newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends flat after rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends flat after rate cuts.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended flat around C$1.3590 (US$0.7358) from Tuesday's close, but rebounded from a session low of C$1.3623 (US$0.7340).
* Unit rebounded from profit-taking after rate cuts by the Bank of Canada and the major commercial banks. * Currency seen trading between C$1.3585 and C$1.3605 overnight.

Canada's central bank cut its key bank rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 4.0 percent, a move which prompted major Canadian banks to drop their prime lending rates to 5.5 percent from 5.75, their lowest level since February 1994.
Traders said the currency's underyling tone remains firm as Canada's economic prospects look good and the issue of Quebec separation remains on the backburner.

The currency was expected to range between C$1.3585 and C$1.3605 overnight. Economists viewed the central bank's move as a bid to ensure that the economy's recent strength continue through 1996 and into 1997.
Other analysts suggested the Bank of Canada was trying to slow the Canadian dollar's recent rally rather than give the economy another boost.

"The message from the Bank of Canada is loud and clear: A strengthening economy is no impediment to lower rates as long as the Canadian dollar is firming," Nesbitt Burns chief economist Sherry Cooper said in a comment.
"While growth is picking up, there is still some slack in the economy," she said in a report.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar firmed to 1.1273 marks from 1.1222 on Tuesday and rose to 82.26 yen from 81.94 yen.
